source.title: Large Neural Networks Learning from Scratch with Very Few Data and without Explicit Regularization

record.tranche_reason: The study compares test performance across CNN architectures with different parameter counts, but does not measure a complete double-descent curve or locate the interpolation threshold.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracies for trained networks of different sizes and training-set sizes. It states that training error is zero in all configurations. It does not report test error over epochs, measurements around an interpolation threshold, or results for label noise or regularization. The SVM comparator results do not test a claim version and are omitted.
record.test_reason: Every configuration is already interpolating: the text says training error is always zero. The study compares three architectures from different families (ResNet018, ResNet101, VGG19), not a size sweep within one family. It never crosses or locates the interpolation threshold, so it cannot show a peak or a second descent (V1, V4), an epoch curve (V2), more data hurting near the threshold (V3), or anything about effective complexity, noise or regularization (V5-V7). It cites Belkin's 'modern interpolation regime' as framing only. Its result is about benign overfitting: interpolating CNNs generalize from few samples. That is a related but different construct, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that very large CNNs trained from scratch with zero training error generalize from very few samples. They say the two larger CNNs consistently beat the smallest, and that more weights can help in these overparameterized regimes. They also say the best architecture depends on the dataset, not the training-set size. They do not frame the results as double descent.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares three distinct CNN architectures on small-data image-classification tasks; it does not reproduce a controlled model-size sweep through the interpolation threshold.
record.method_sensitivity: The relative architecture ranking varies by dataset; the authors report ResNet101 best in 6 of 8 cases and VGG19 best in 2 of 8 cases.

fits_no_version.finding: Interpolating CNNs (11-140M parameters, zero training error, no regularization, augmentation or pretraining) reach well-above-chance test accuracy with 10-67 samples per class. The two larger architectures beat ResNet018 in most cases, but parameter count does not order performance: ResNet101 is best in 6 of 8 cases. The architecture ranking is stable across training-set sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign overfitting: heavily overparameterized networks that interpolate small training sets still generalize, and larger architectures often, but not always, generalize better.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning and Computing (2022)
record.problems: Only three distinct architectures are compared, and they differ in more than parameter count. The study does not trace a controlled size sweep around the interpolation threshold. Results are limited to CNN image-classification settings. Several reported accuracies are means over 5 models, with standard deviations; the text also notes that Caltech subsets differ across seeds.
record.rows_left_out: The StanfordCars numerical entries in Table 3 are absent from the supplied text, so no numerical rows were recoverable for that dataset. Figure-only curve values without exact textual numbers were not added as separate measurements. SVM baseline values in Tables 3 and 4 were omitted because they are not deep-network size results.

untested.parts: Whole version: there is no size sweep through the interpolation threshold and no peak; only three architectures, all interpolating.
No test error is reported over epochs.
Sample size varies, but only far past interpolation (accuracy rises with data); no runs near the threshold.
No curve crosses the interpolation point; there is no classical regime.
No label noise, multiple peaks or regularization tuning.
No effective parameter count is used.

missing.what: StanfordCars accuracies are present in the text, contrary to rows_left_out. At 20 per class: ResNet018 5.50, ResNet101 6.79, VGG19 4.72. At about 42 per class: 20.33, 24.34, 16.14. SVM comparator 69.5. These are relevant to the benign-overfitting finding.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and its V1 limits_scope label are not supported: the rows cannot show any double-descent shape because no measurement sits at or below the interpolation threshold, and the architectures differ in more than size. The SVM comparator values were rightly excluded as cited results.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not trace a size sweep through the interpolation threshold or report the predicted fall-rise-fall curve; it compares a few different architectures in highly overparameterized settings.
Test performance over training epochs is not reported.
Although training-set sizes vary, the study does not identify settings near the interpolation threshold or test whether more data raises test error there.
No general double-descent curve is tested across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure or prediction of peak location is evaluated.
Label noise, multiple peaks, and optimally tuned regularization are not tested.
The study does not recalculate complexity using an effective parameter count or test whether that yields an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.operation_detail: Compare architectures with different parameter counts after training.
rows.note: Mean of 5 models; an individual architecture score does not establish a double-descent curve.
rows.check: Table 3 cross-architecture accuracies, all in the zero-training-error regime. There is no within-family size sweep and no interpolation threshold, so these rows cannot bear on a model-wise double-descent curve. Accuracy is also not monotone in parameter count: VGG19 is below ResNet101 on CUB and Flowers102.

rows.value: ResNet101 best in 6 of 8 cases; VGG19 best in 2 of 8 cases; ResNet018 has the worst results on the fine-grained tasks

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Tested highly overparameterized CNN architecture comparisons
reader_labels.reason: The results compare only a few different architectures, and the best-performing size varies by dataset; they do not establish the full size-wise fall-rise-fall shape (r19-r37).
